name: Lucifer of Cagliari
otherNames: Luciferus; Lucifer Calaritanus (the Latin forms; Calaris is Cagliari)
knownFor: The bishop of Cagliari who defied the emperor over Athanasius, and whose refusal to forgive former Arians began the Luciferian schism.
role: Bishop, polemicist and leader of a schism

keyWorks.title: Pamphlets against Constantius (On Apostate Kings; On not holding communion with heretics; and others)
keyWorks.about: the hard Nicene attacks on the emperor's church policy, written in exile; the Latin texts survive

traces: The Luciferian party, which broke with the wider church over whether former Arians could be forgiven; Jerome says it outlived him, and Theodoret of Cyrrhus says it later faded.
remembered: Jerome wrote a Dialogue against the Luciferians about 379, granting Lucifer's courage against the Arians while rejecting his schism.
His consecration of Paulinus at Antioch, Socrates of Constantinople says, deepened a split there that lasted for years.

uncertain: How far Lucifer was a true schismatic is not clear. Jerome calls him a good shepherd and a saintly man, yet blames the schism on him; Ambrose and Augustine, Fremantle's edition notes, speak of him as having fallen into schism.
His date of death is given as about 370 or 371; Jerome's Chronicle gives 371.
The reports that he acted out of love of glory, or out of a grudge against Eusebius of Vercelli, Jerome says he does not believe.
